title: A super-simple way to organize your internet
author: David Pierce

recommendations.name: Starfield
recommendations.blurb: A big, huge, epic, giant, massive sci-fi game that actually seems to live up to the hype. This is more of an “explore the universe” kind of game than a “shoot the bad guy” game, but that’s all the more reason you might find yourself spending way too many hours playing.

recommendations.name: Can You Start a YouTube channel in 2023?
recommendations.blurb: Can You Start a YouTube channel in 2023? I could watch Marques Brownlee and Cleo Abram talk about the mechanics of running and growing a YouTube channel for hours.

recommendations.name: Obscura 4
recommendations.blurb: I’ve always been kind of dubious of custom iPhone camera apps — the built-in one is good and so much easier to access and more reliable — but the new Obscura has me reconsidering. ( MacStories has a good breakdown of everything that’s new.)

recommendations.name: The Big Flop: Quibi Bites the Dust
recommendations.blurb: It’s so perfect and funny that you can tell the whole story of Quibi in one 37-minute podcast episode that is actually mostly just jokes about Quibi’s bad shows. But this is actually a pretty good recap and — call me crazy! — sort of convinced me that Quibi didn’t miss by too much.

recommendations.name: One Piece on Netflix
recommendations.blurb: The long-awaited live-action remake of One Piece, a popular manga and anime series, now has its full first season streaming on Netflix.

recommendations.name: Aboard
recommendations.blurb: A new app from Rich Ziade and Paul Ford, two people who tend to make good apps. The best way I can describe this one is “Trello meets Pinterest meets Google Sheets” — you can just dump in URLs, notes, images, spreadsheets, whatever, and organize it all in one place, alone or with others.

recommendations.name: The Making of Karateka
recommendations.blurb: It’s a documentary, and also a video game, about the making of a video game. (The Verge’s Andrew Webster wrote a great story about it this week.)

recommendations.name: Ollie’s Arcade
recommendations.blurb: Big week for old video games! This new iOS app is just a simple store for some simple retro games — so far, Snake, Ollie Soars (a Flappy Bird-style game), and a space-explorer game called Tranquility Touchdown. No ads, no sneaky subscriptions, just fun games for a couple bucks.

recommendations.name: The Analog Weekly planner
recommendations.blurb: I’ve been a fan of Jeff Sheldon and Ugmonk for a long time, and the standard Analog productivity system is one of those ridiculously luxurious things — it’s just paper and a paper holder, and it’s expensive! — that feels totally worth it.

recommendations.name: Raindrop.io
recommendations.blurb: I use an app called Raindrop.io, which works on basically every platform, integrates really easily with other apps, and makes saving super easy. I’ll dump a URL in there, rename the weird page title to “Kaiden’s volleyball schedule,” and it’s right there next time I need it.

recommendations.name: Anybox
recommendations.blurb: If you’re an Apple user looking for something a little sleeker (Raindrop is… not the best-looking app), you can use apps like Anybox or GoodLinks. GoodLinks is better if you’re also going to use it as a place to store and read articles, but Anybox is the more powerful organizer.

recommendations.name: Evernote
recommendations.blurb: You can use a lot of note-taking apps as link buckets: Evernote, OneNote, and Notion all have good web clippers and good search, and you can have everything from Obsidian to Bear to Amplenote grab the full text of a page and save it for later.

recommendations.name: Pocket
recommendations.blurb: Read-later apps also fall into the not-exactly-right-but-does-work category. I don’t love Pocket as a reading app anymore, but as a place to save links and search through them later, it does fine; so does Instapaper. Anything with full-text search should do the job.

recommendations.name: EXIST
recommendations.blurb: EXIST is EXO’s newly released seventh album.

recommendations.name: Cream Soda
recommendations.blurb: It’s a groovy summery album, and the title track, “ Cream Soda,” is a bop. (The B-sides “ Hear Me Out ” and “ Let Me In ” are also great.) Why else do you think I have an EXO wallpaper at the moment?

recommendations.name: Junk journaling videos
recommendations.blurb: Junk journaling videos are so oddly soothing and satisfying.

recommendations.name: Gentler Streak
recommendations.blurb: The default fitness app for iOS has the ring system, but more than motivation, it can feel like a punishment. Say, if I am sick one day and I need a rest, there is no way I can pause the ring. Gentler Streak takes a new approach to workouts with intervals in between to rest.

recommendations.name: Voyager for Lemmy
recommendations.blurb: Voyager for Lemmy: If you were a Reddit user using Apollo, this app makes Lemmy feel right at home. What I like about this is because it’s a web app, I can use it on all my devices for a consistent experience.

recommendations.name: Cinny
recommendations.blurb: Thank you so much for recommending Beeper. I’ve been following Matrix for a while now — from what I can tell, ActivityPub has the apps, but Matrix’s source code has more potential.

recommendations.name: t2bot.io
recommendations.blurb: Thank you so much for recommending Beeper. I’ve been following Matrix for a while now — from what I can tell, ActivityPub has the apps, but Matrix’s source code has more potential.

recommendations.name: Forté by Twelve South
recommendations.blurb: Loved the Zen Magsafe stand, but I feel like my favorite version of this (which is about to get very important given the new ‘StandBy mode’ coming to iOS 17) is the Forté by Twelve South. It’s so clean and elegant that Apple actually used it in its own promotional stuff.

recommendations.name: Reeder
recommendations.blurb: I’ve been trying our Reeder. I know it’s not a new app, but I’m trying to fill the news void I have since leaving Twitter with RSS.

recommendations.name: Capacities
recommendations.blurb: Capacities! I found a great recommendation from a thread by Casey Newton related to the tinkerpaloozaas that are most personal knowledge managers. Capacities has a fresh approach. Fun and free to try!

recommendations.name: Casey Newton (@crumbler) on Threads

recommendations.name: Pocket Glow in the Dark
recommendations.blurb: I’m losing my mind over the fact that Analogue is releasing a glow-in-the-dark Pocket. Even though I already own one, I’m tempted to buy this version just because glow-in-the-dark is way cooler than the clear plastic trend that’s currently making a comeback.

recommendations.name: Molecano
recommendations.blurb: Molecano is a cute little mobile game that has elements of both the NYT Spelling Bee and Scrabble. I’ve now played an ungodly number of levels.

recommendations.name: Siri Shortcuts
recommendations.blurb: Obsessively into Siri Shortcuts automations: Open Instagram, lowers my media volume (no more autoplay scares); Open YouTube/daycare livestream, turns off orientation lock (and vice versa); Battery percentages trigger low power (30%) or normal power mode (80%); 10:00pm triggers grayscale color…
